Chapter 8. The Cost of Silence.
You know that hush that settles over a room when a tough subject comes up—and everyone just lets it slide by? That silence can feel so much easier in the moment. At home, at work, or out in public, it’s tempting to keep things smooth and comfortable. But here’s something we don’t always realize: silence comes with a price tag. And all too often, the people who pay are the ones already struggling to get their voices heard.
Picture a teacher who knows some of their students face real challenges. They want to help, but when it comes to talking about race in class, they freeze up. What if parents get upset? What if they say the wrong thing? What if trying to help just makes things worse? So, they let it go. The topic gets skipped, and those students are left to figure things out on their own.
Most of us don’t even notice how silence shapes what’s possible. If we never say the word “racism,” how do we fight it? If we don’t share stories, it’s way too easy for people to believe there’s no problem at all. When we stay quiet, injustice can just keep going—hidden, unchallenged, and unchecked.
Think about a friend who’s always been the one to speak up. After a while, they get tired. They watch as people laugh at the same old jokes, repeat stereotypes, and let chances to do better slip by. Eventually, even they stop speaking. That silence? It just gets heavier. And that feeling of being alone? It only grows.
The real cost of silence isn’t just personal—it’s something we all share. When we’re too afraid to talk about race, the space for real change gets smaller. Conversations get shallow. Solutions don’t go deep enough. If we want real progress, honesty’s a must—even when it makes us squirm.
Here’s the thing: breaking the silence takes guts. It’s not about having all the right words, or never slipping up. It’s about being willing to start the conversation, to really listen, and to keep learning. That’s how we break the cycle of denial and avoidance—and finally start moving things forward.
